blocks.text: GLOSSARY 333

Cc
camerate: distinctive cross-banding found in some chaetae of
Orbiniidae.
capillary chaeta: slender, often long, chaeta tapering to a fine
point.
capillary, capillaries: see capillary chaeta.
caruncle: projection from the posterior end of the prostomium
carrying nuchal organs.
cauda: posterior end in Sabellariidae.
cephalic cage: long, forwardly directed chaetae enclosing the
head, as in some Flabelligeridae.
cephalic keel: median ridge on the prostomium or head, as in
some Maldanidae.
cephalic plaque: plate-like antero-dorsal surface of the head
region in some Maldanidae. Also called cephalic plate.
cephalic veil: Smooth or fringed structure surrounding the

buccal region in Pectinariidae. Probably comprising the pros-
tomium and peristomium.

cephalization: incorporation or modification of anterior seg-
ments to form a head.

ceratophore: basal part of an antenna.
ceratostyle: distal part of an antenna.

chaeta, chaetae: a chitinous bristle protruding from an epider-
mal pocket in the body wall.

chaetal inversion: presence of uncini on the notopodia, rather
than the more usual position on the neuropodia.
chaetiger: segment bearing chaetae.

chaetigerous lobe: that projection or part of the notopodium
or neuropodium that bears the chaetae.

chaetoblast: cell that forms, together with follicle cells, a
chaeta.

chemoautotroph: organism able to synthesize organic nutri-
ents from inorganic sources, excluding photosynthesis.

chevron: V-shaped chitinized jaw piece at the base of the pro-
boscis in some Goniadidae.

chlorocruorin: respiratory blood pigment; changes in colour
from green to red with increasing concentration.

chromatophil gland: densely staining gland in the ventral pin-
nule of Tomopteris; see also rosette gland.

chromatophore: special cell or group of cells carrying pigment.
ciliophore: distinct area or epidermal patch covered with cilia.

circular muscle: muscle layer encircling the body between the
epidermis and longitudinal muscle layer.

circumoesophageal connective: tracts of nervous tissue pass-
ing down from the brain on either side of the foregut and
connecting to the ventral nerve cord.
cirriform: slender and cylindrical.
cirrophore: basal projection on which a cirrus is mounted.
cirrostyle: distal part of a cirrus.
cirrus, cir

parapodial appendages; usually slender and
cylindrical, can be elongate on anterior segments of some
Phyllodocida (see anterior cirri). Also refers to peristomial
structures in some Eunicidae.
clade: a common ancestor and all its descendants.
cladistics: systematics based on discovering synapomorphies to
group organisms, in principle, recognizing only clades as taxa.
clitellum: a thickened glandular area, that secrets a cocoon or
egg capsule in Clitellata. The clitellum is located over several
segments in the anterior third of the body.
coelom, coelomate: body cavity often with a peritoneal lin-

ing; formed in embryonic mesoderm; characteristic of many
bilateral animals.

coelomoduct: a tubule derived from mesodermal tissue, con-
necting the coelom with the external environment and may
have a coelomostome; said to combine with a nephridium and
termed nephromixia or mixonephridia.
coelomostome: funnel at the inner end of a coelomoduct.

cold seep: emergence of fluid from sedimentary rocks under
pressure, such as in regions of continental subduction; may
comprise hydrocarbons, such as methane, or water, bearing
salts such as sulphides.
collar: anterior encircling fold or flap, such as that covering the
base of the radiolar crown in Sabellidae.
comb chaeta: simple chaeta with a comb-like arrangement of
teeth on the distal end; present in some Eunicida.

commensalism: an association between two species that live
together, which benefits individuals of one species without
harming those of the other. |
commissure: a transverse band of neural tissue linking paired
ventral nerves or longitudinal nerve tracks; also, one of four
main tracts of nervous tissue passing through the brain.

companion chaetae: small, simple chaetae, accompanying, or
alternating with larger chaetae, usually hooks of some kind.

compound chaeta: chaeta having a terminal portion that artic-
ulates with the shaft.
compressed: flattened in one plane, usually laterally.

corpora pedunculata: paired dorso-laterally situated
mushroom-shaped bodies in the brain of Aphroditiformia,
Nereididae, Hesionoidea, possibly Nephtyidae and Serpulidae.
crown: a bilaterally symmetrical branched structure in some
annelids (Oweniidae, Sabellida) formed by prostomial palps.

ctenidia: small ciliated pads on the notopodia between the
elytrophores or dorsal tubercles and the notochaetae, or on
the parapodia of some scale-worms.

ctenognaths: Eunicida in which the jaws comprise relative-
ly large basal maxillae and symmetrically arranged rows of
numerous anterior denticles in longitudinal series without
carriers.
cupule, cupules: fused pair or pairs of notopodia in anteri-
or body of some Chaetopteridae, appearing as an elaborate
cup-shape.
